topics.label: Introduction to the Hallmarks of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's learning outcomes, contextualises cancer mechanisms within previous lectures, and outlines the hallmarks of cancer framework.

topics.label: Sustained Proliferation and Growth Signal Independence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how mutations in cell surface receptors and intracellular signaling cascades drive continuous cancer cell proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Blockade of Cellular Differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells fail to withdraw from the cell cycle and arrest during differentiation in both hematological malignancies and solid carcinomas.

topics.label: Resistance to Apoptotic Cell Death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how genetic disruption of the p53 pathway and altered balances between pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins allow tumor cells to evade cell death.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality and Senescence Bypass
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover telomere shortening, the mechanism of telomerase reactivation in cancer cells, and the cellular stress pathways governing senescence.

topics.label: Deregulation of Cellular Metabolism
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore cancer metabolic reprogramming, including the Warburg effect, diagnostic glucose uptake, and the role of oncometabolites in altering gene expression.

topics.label: Induction of Tumor Angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the necessity of new blood vessel growth for supplying tumors with oxygen and nutrients and examines the regulatory balance driving the angiogenic switch.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Genetics of Cancer Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the metastatic cascade, diagnostic tracking through lymph nodes and circulating tumor cells, microenvironmental compatibility, and the clonal genetics of dissemination.

topics.label: Conclusion and Lecture Summary
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer wraps up the lecture by reviewing the integration of cancer hallmarks, discussing further reading, and framing the upcoming practical sessions.
